judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals are descriptive and contain no operative term needing construction, though the phrase 'no-cost assignable option' is loose and the boilerplate consideration recital ($10 plus 'other good and valuable consideration') is formulaic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital that Optionee 'requires a no-cost assignable option' sits somewhat awkwardly against operative ¶12 and ¶8, which impose real costs on Optionor and a $50,000 reimbursement obligation on Optionee, but no direct contradiction with ¶1 or ¶3 appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'approximately 10.89 acres' and the reliance on a legal description 'more particularly described in' Exhibit 1 leave the Property's extent soft, and 'exclusive and irrevocable' states no duration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against ¶2's 'not less than one (1) year' term, ¶13's assignment consent scheme, and Exhibit 3 ¶1 which says '10.89 acres' without 'approximately' and points to Attachment A rather than Exhibit 1 — a mild descriptive mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall continue in effect for a period of not less than one (1) year' sets a floor with no ceiling, so the Option's 'expiration' — the very date by which exercise must occur — is left genuinely uncertain, a textbook lexical/mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with ¶14 (termination on failure to exercise 'within the time ... provided herein'), ¶9 (closing 90 days after exercise) and ¶20 (deemed receipt), and the open-ended term cannot be reconciled with those time-bound provisions or with ¶21's time-of-the-essence clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause mixes an illustrative 'For example' with operative numbers, defines 'Outstanding Balance' by reference to 'deductions as described below' that are scattered elsewhere, and makes payment depend on TIF reimbursement 'received by Developer' — who is not yet a party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with ¶4 (conveyance 'upon payment of the Purchase Price, less the Outstanding Balance'), ¶8's $500,000 deduction and ¶12's retention of the Outstanding Balance by Optionee, and those provisions do not cleanly say who owes the balance after assignment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'good and marketable indefeasible fee simple title ... free and clear of all liens and encumbrances whatsoever, subject only to those items ('Permitted Exceptions') set forth in Exhibit 1' is internally tensioned but the terms are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶6 defines 'Permitted Exceptions' quite differently — as conditions not objected to or accepted by Optionee — so the same defined term has two sources, a real internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed, dated and standard-referenced survey obligations; 'such Table A items as Optionee may elect' is open but is a deliberate election, not an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The December 31, 2006 updated-survey date sits alongside ¶12's December 1, 2006 Brownfield deadline and its four 30-day extensions, but the two are not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence switches to 'Seller' and 'Purchaser', parties never defined in this instrument, and duplicates the same 30-day deadline already stated — a drafting slip that could be argued about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against ¶4's title covenant and ¶6's second paragraph defining Permitted Exceptions, and the undefined Seller/Purchaser labels appear to be imported from Exhibit 1's purchase agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the option of either (1) ... (2) ... (3)' offers three alternatives after 'either', and option (3) ends with a competing right 'at Optionor's discretion', so who actually chooses is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its definition of 'Permitted Exceptions' conflicts with ¶4, which locates Permitted Exceptions in Exhibit 1, and option (2) extends cure 'during the term of the Option' which is itself open-ended under ¶2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard ownership-and-authority representation with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with ¶22 (Authority of Optionor), except that ¶22 speaks of partnerships while the preamble identifies an LLC — a mismatch located in ¶22, not here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A knowledge-qualified representation; 'no knowledge of any reason why the local governmental authorities would not allow' is soft, but knowledge qualifiers are ordinary drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with ¶12, which acknowledges numerous approvals are still required, so the representation is qualified rather than contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'of sufficient size, capacity' and 'without any special charge, assessment or apparatus for its current use' are vague — sufficient for what use, and 'its current use' is unspecified against the contemplated federal facility.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The reference to 'current use' sits oddly with ¶12's utility relocation contemplated for the new development, but no operative provision squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A disclosure representation tied to a statutory definition; 'all environmental information that it has' is broad but self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the carve-out expressly referenced in ¶7(e) and drives ¶8's Due Care mechanics, and the pieces fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'to the best of Optionor's actual knowledge' and a sweeping list of laws is standard environmental representation language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Schedule A and ¶7(d) exceptions are expressly incorporated, and Schedule A is listed among the attachments, so the cross-references hold.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow factual representation about historic use; the list is specific and no catch-all creates scope doubt.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by ¶7(d)'s admission that the property is a statutory 'facility' with contaminating historic uses, which is an express carve-out rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence 'The exemptions include that owner's obligations to comply with its due care requirements' is garbled — exemptions do not 'include' obligations — and the conditional framing makes the representation hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It links to ¶8's Due Care/MCL 324.20107a scheme and the ¶7(d) 'facility' disclosure, which together largely absorb the point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward bring-down language, though 'until and including any exercise of this Option' stops short of closing, which a party could argue about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because ¶2 makes exercise convert Exhibit 1 into a binding purchase contract, the truncation of the bring-down at exercise rather than closing is a real, if modest, seam between ¶7 and Exhibit 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonably cooperate', 'best efforts to obtain the maximum allowable reimbursable costs' and 'most cost effective and appropriate' are vague standards, but the allocation of responsibility is stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with ¶12's Brownfield Plan paragraphs, which also assign Eligible Activities listing to Optionee, and the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the unapproved amount not to exceed $500,000' labelled 'Limitation of Liability' is reasonably clear, though whether the cap is per event or aggregate is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same Limitation of Liability cap is invoked again in ¶12's reduced-Eligible-Activities paragraph, raising a genuine question whether the $500,000 is one cap or two separate deductions from the Outstanding Balance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite deadline measured from exercise, with venue left to Exhibit 1; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on ¶2's exercise mechanics and ¶20's deemed-receipt rules, but adds no inconsistency of its own.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence is ungrammatical ('Optionee will have an opportunity to inspect the Property and that the Property will be conveyed'), and 'as is' condition 'except as otherwise provided' leaves the carve-out unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An 'as is' conveyance sits in tension with the affirmative title and environmental representations in ¶7 and the clean-title covenant in ¶4, and with Exhibit 1's unseen terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any other due diligence matters deemed reasonably prudent' is a catch-all after a specific list, and 'reasonable notice' and 'insurance in amounts ... reasonably acceptable' are undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The entry right runs 'during the period of this Option including any extension periods', which inherits ¶2's open-ended term, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 'may include, but not be limited to' list of seven approvals is followed by an Optionor responsibility limited to street vacations and zoning variances, leaving who bears the other listed approvals genuinely open (expressio unius against the catch-all).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The later ¶12 paragraphs assign Brownfield Plan work to Optionor and Eligible Activities to Optionee, which fills some but not all of the gap left here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as soon as practical' and 'a final determination of those costs' are undefined trigger points for a termination right, and 'any other public roads' is loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The termination right here is an additional exit not mentioned in ¶14, which frames termination solely around failure to exercise — a mild whole-instrument seam.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'purchase the Site' uses a term defined nowhere in the Option (the defined term is 'Property'), and 'use its best efforts to secure funds to reimburse' is a soft, appropriations-contingent promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This surviving reimbursement obligation is hard to square with ¶14, which says that on non-exercise the Option terminates 'without further action or obligation on the part of either party'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'provide its support and written consent when required' is vague about what triggers the duty, but the approval mechanics are otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits ¶12's allocation of approval responsibilities and ¶12's Brownfield approval paragraph without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'must be reasonable and necessary to affect Optionee's intended use' uses 'affect' for 'effect' and states a soft standard, but the drafting duties are clearly allocated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with ¶8 (Optionee estimates Eligible Activity costs) though ¶8 places the estimating burden on Optionee while this paragraph adds Optionor 'assistance' — a small overlap, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'obtain approval of the Brownfield Plan for the project prior to Optionee by no later than December 1, 2006' is garbled — 'prior to Optionee' has no referent — and 'so long as the delays are not caused by the Optionor' sits oddly with an extension exercisable by Optionor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The December 1, 2006 deadline plus four 30-day extensions interacts with ¶12's later paragraph on retention of the Outstanding Balance if the Plan is not approved before Closing, and with ¶2's minimum one-year term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'that amount (up to the Limitation of Liability) shall be deducted' is ambiguous as to whether 'that amount' means the approved amount or the shortfall, which changes the deduction entirely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reuses ¶8's $500,000 'Limitation of Liability' for a second, different deduction against the Outstanding Balance, leaving unclear whether the cap is aggregate across ¶8 and ¶12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'retained by Optionee' is odd on its own terms, since under ¶3 the Outstanding Balance is payable to Optionor out of TIF proceeds received by the Developer, not held by Optionee.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to reconcile with ¶3 and ¶4, which make the Outstanding Balance a deferred Developer payment stream rather than escrowed funds in Optionee's hands, and with ¶13's assignment of the Option to the Developer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'further assignment only with the prior written consent of the original Optionee' and 'in it sole discretion' (typo) are workable, though 'This Option may be assigned ... without the consent of the Optionor' is unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶1 limits assignment to 'Optionee's developer' prior to closing, while this paragraph permits assignment generally without Optionor consent — a genuine, if narrow, tension between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If Optionee elects not to exercise' makes termination turn on an unexpressed election rather than the passage of time, and 'without further action or obligation on the part of either party' is an unqualified sweep of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It collides with ¶12's promise that if the Developer does not execute the purchase agreement Optionee will use best efforts to reimburse up to $50,000 in traffic-study costs, and with ¶2's open-ended 'not less than one (1) year' term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph contains scanning/typing errors ('ferninine', 'the particular portion I which such word is used'), but the interpretive rules it states are conventional and the sense survives.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere — including ¶13's assignment terms — turns on partnership or agency status, so it is coherent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all acts as may be necessary' and documents 'in the form and substance satisfactory to the parties and their respective counsel' are broad, and the last sentence could swallow the obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports ¶16-style release recordings tied to Exhibit 3's recorded Memorandum, and no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure boilerplate with a definite operation and no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the Option or Exhibit 3 bears on execution formalities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The integration clause is clear, though it says the parties' agreements are 'embodied in this Option and Exhibit 1' while elsewhere naming Exhibit 3 as one of the only agreements — an internal wobble in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It omits Exhibit 2 (Survey) and Schedule A, both of which the Option incorporates by reference in ¶5 and ¶7(e), so the enumeration of documents is incomplete against the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as provided in the Act, all disputes arising under or relating to this Option shall be resolved under this Act' is slightly circular, but the CDA reference is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names the same Contracting Officer as ¶20's notice address, so the two are consistent; the naming of an individual could be argued about if he left office.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause lists three delivery methods but supplies deemed-receipt rules only for mail and courier, leaving personal delivery unaddressed, and 'or is addressed in such other way as the parties may from time to time direct' is loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶2 makes exercise effective 'on the date of the receipt of notice ... as provided in Section 20', so the deemed-receipt gap here directly bears on when the Option is exercised and when Exhibit 1 becomes binding.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard time-of-the-essence clause with a clear weekend/holiday rule; nothing in it is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Time of the essence is hard to reconcile with ¶2's open-ended 'not less than one (1) year' term, and with ¶12's Optionor-controlled extensions of the Brownfield deadline.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause demands a corporate resolution or partnership approvals but the Optionor is a Michigan limited liability company, so the required deliverable does not match the entity — a drafting mismatch.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble and Exhibit 3's acknowledgment identify Optionor as an LLC acting through a Managing Member, which this paragraph's corporate/partnership formula does not fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital-style identification of the parties with only typographical noise; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Option's own preamble in date, parties and addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'containing 10.89 acres' is stated as exact and the Option is described as 'is fully assignable', both slightly firmer than the underlying grant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶1 of the Option says 'approximately 10.89 acres' and describes the Property by reference to Exhibit 1, whereas this recorded Memorandum uses Attachment A — a recorded description that may not match the operative one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It repeats verbatim the 'not less than one (1) year' formulation, which fixes a minimum but no expiration date, so the recorded instrument gives public notice of an option of indeterminate duration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is meant to mirror ¶2 of the Option and does so, but that means the same open-ended term now appears in a recorded document, compounding rather than resolving the ¶2/¶14 problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short statement of recording purpose with a definite meaning and no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reference to 'the Optionee or its assignee' is consistent with ¶1 and ¶13 of the Option on assignment.
